classification_signals: In this paper we explore the possibilities that portable Electroencephalography (EEG) technology offers in order to understand the behaviour of pedestrians in a specific nocturnal urban aural environment. Previous EEG research conducted in urban design has shown links between environmental cues and mood-enhancement (Aspinall et al., 2013). In the current pre-pilot project we recorded EEG data of stationary participants while they were exposed to urban soundscapes along a chosen pathway. Our intention was to investigate links between these soundscapes and the impact they have on the listeners’ emotional state. Analysis of the data revealed probable evidence that the distance between the sound source and the listener generates feelings of discomfort. More particularly proximity of the sound source showed rise in frustration. Based on our findings we propose the design of a responsive brain interface. The paper finally discusses theories of environmental psychology, neuroscience, sound perception and affective computing.
title: The City Soundscape and the Brain

our recording methods were not very accurate when it came to the synchronization of the sound files with the EEG recordings with a divergence of a couple of seconds.
Wilcoxon signed rank test but the conclusions were inconclusive.

discrepancy detected could be interpreted as a random event; participant A could have had high levels of arousal on the day of the experiment, prior to our actual testing.
Edinburgh has cold temperatures during springtime and especially during night hours, this could have been another reason that arousal was high for that specific participant.
Most importantly though we should take into account some aspects of “distance hearing” that we missed in our analysis.

minimum_safe_summary: This pre-pilot empirical study investigated the relationship between urban soundscapes and pedestrians' emotional states using portable EEG technology. Findings suggest that closer proximity to sound sources increases frustration levels, and a responsive brain interface designed to distance sound sources in real-time successfully reduced overall frustration. Limitations include the small sample size, pre-pilot stage, and technical challenges with EEG data streaming and sound synchronization, highlighting the need for further research with larger samples and improved methodologies to better understand individual differences in sound perception and emotional responses.

theory_commitments.specific_claim: Urban environments, particularly their soundscapes, may hinder directed attention restoration and contribute to psychological discomfort.

mechanism_chain.description: Perceived sound intensity, mediated by distance, leads to physiological arousal and subsequent feelings of discomfort.
